entities.name: WEE1
observations: Nuclear WEE1 protein was assessed by immunohistochemistry in 287 ovarian carcinoma effusions; 265/287 (92%) were positive, with Western blot positivity in 45/45 tested samples.
High WEE1 expression was defined as >25% of tumor cells and was associated with higher expression in post-chemotherapy recurrence effusions than pretreatment effusions (p=0.002).

entities.name: Ovarian serous carcinoma
observations: The direct evidence concerns advanced FIGO III–IV ovarian serous carcinoma effusions, not all ovarian carcinoma specimens.
In the full 287-effusion cohort, high WEE1 expression showed only a trend toward poorer overall survival (p=0.083).

entities.name: WEE1 poor survival
observations: Among 109 patients with post-chemotherapy effusions, high WEE1 expression was associated with poorer overall survival in univariate analysis (p=0.004).
High WEE1 remained independently prognostic in multivariable Cox analysis adjusted for clinicopathologic variables (p=0.003).
The accessible abstract does not report a hazard ratio or confidence interval.
No separate primary validation cohort for this specific post-chemotherapy effusion setting was identified.

entities.name: PMID:25093290
observations: Slipicevic et al., Gynecologic Oncology (2014), reported that WEE1 is an independent prognostic marker of poor survival in post-chemotherapy ovarian carcinoma effusions.
